script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

Title: Finding New Roots

INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. CAROLINE DAVENPORT (40s, warm, practical) stirs a large pot of oatmeal on the stove, humming a familiar tune. Her husband JOSH (50s, rugged, silent) sits at the table, reading the newspaper.

MRS. CAROLINE
(cheerfully)
Good morning, dear. Are you ready for another day on the farm?

JOSH
(distracted)
Yes, I suppose so.

MRS. CAROLINE
(smiling)
I know it's not the most exciting work, but it pays the bills. And it keeps us close to our children.

JOSH
(frustrated)
I know. I just feel like there's more to life than this.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

The family sits in the living room. CAROLINE's eldest daughter EMMA (18, ambitious, confident) is reading a newspaper, while her younger brother SAM (14, curious, energetic) plays with LEGOs on the floor.

CAROLINE
(looking at an old photograph)
Do you remember when we first moved here? You were just a baby, Sam. Your father and I were both excited to start a new life on this farm.

EMMA
(sarcastically)
Yeah, I've heard that story a million times.

SAM
(interrupting)
Was there a pony, Mom?

CAROLINE
(laughing)
No, Sam. But we did have a beautiful garden. Your father was so proud of it.

JOSH
(entering, frowning)
I can't take this anymore. I need a change.

EMMA
(surprised)
What do you mean?

JOSH
I can't keep living like this. I need to find a new career, something that challenges me.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JOSH sits in a coffee shop, nursing a cup of coffee. His friend MIKE (50s, wise, supportive) joins him.

MIKE
You look troubled, old friend. What's going on?

JOSH
I can't take the farm anymore. I need a change, something new.

MIKE
(nodding)
I understand. But have you considered what that change would be?

JOSH
I don't know. I just know I can't keep doing this.

MIKE
(thoughtfully)
Have you thought about going back to school? There's a great community college just outside of town. They offer a wide range of programs.

INT. FARMHOUSE LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the TV, watching the evening news. CAROLINE looks concerned as she hears about a nearby factory closing down, leaving many workers unemployed.

EMMA
(angrily)
This is ridiculous. Another factory closing? How are people supposed to survive?

JOSH
(suddenly inspired)
I have an idea.

INT. COLLEGE CAMPUS - DAY

JOSH sits in a classroom, surrounded by young students. He looks determined as he takes notes.

EXT. FARMHOUSE - NIGHT

The family sits outside on the porch, watching the sunset. JOSH looks content, knowing that he has finally found a new path for his career.

CAROLINE
(proudly)
I'm so proud of you, dear. You're finally following your dreams.

JOSH
(smiling)
It's never too late to make a change.

EMMA
(smiling back)
That's what I'm going to do too.

SAM
(excitedly)
Can I come with you to the factory, Dad?

JOSH
(laughing)
Of course, Sam.

The family shares a loving moment as they look towards the future, knowing that together they can face any challenge.

FADE OUT.
